english.title: Wrongful disclosure of personal information to a person who is not a relevant official / Minister of the Crown
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being

(A)_[a person who was a relevant official,]_
(B)_[the Secretary of State by whom general customs functions were exercisable,]_
(C)_[a Minister in the Secretary of State department by whom general customs functions were exercisable,]_

wrongfully disclosed personal customs information to a person who was not a

(D)_[relevant official,]_
(E)_[Minister of the Crown in that department,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), in contravention of section 15(1) of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009
english.legislation: Contrary to section 15(1) and 18 of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009

english.notes:
(i) Section 18(2) of the Act provides that it is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to prove that the person reasonably believed - (a) that the disclosure was lawful, or
(b) that the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public.
(ii) Section 18(3) provides that a prosecution for an offence under this section may be brought in England and Wales only with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Director of Revenue and Customs Prosecutions
(iii) Section 18(4) provides that this section is without prejudice to the pursuit of any remedy or the taking of any action in relation to a breach of section 15(1) or (2) or 17(1) (whether or not this section applies to the breach).
(iv) Section 16 contains a number of exceptions to this offence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 18(5) and (6) of the Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
